acceptanceCriteria: A benchmark over a representative 87KB receipt and a 13KB native report is retained before and after.

Every existing secretscreen match and redaction test passes unchanged, and a differential test shows the faster path returns the same match set as Pattern on a retained corpus including all current positive fixtures.
internal/testacceptance and internal/behaviorfalsify hosted race times are retained before and after.
body: Observed 2026-10-04 while diagnosing V1-0715 (Core 1.0.0-rc.1 build 163) at origin/main 2ffb4c53, darwin/arm64, go1.27.1. Confirmed measurement, optimization. secretscreen.Pattern scans at about 1 microsecond per byte: one MatchString over an 87,204-byte encoded behaviorfalsify EvidenceReceipt took 101-113ms, a 12,673-byte native report 14ms; under -race the same scans took 2.15s and 0.3s (about 22 microseconds per byte). Pattern.MatchString instead of FindAllStringIndex made no material difference (96ms vs 101ms), so the cost is the NFA over the large case-insensitive alternation, not match collection. behaviorfalsify.VerifyReceipt re-encodes and screens the receipt on every call: plan preimage, every hook and native byte field (raw text, each decoded JSON string, each key=value), then the encoded document again with the same bytes as base64; one verify of a 4-attempt receipt took 462ms without race. A CPU profile of TestPTFV0ParentCompleteAttemptOutcome under race attributed about 47% of samples to secretscreen.writerMatches. Expected: screening cost that does not dominate receipt verification. Candidate directions, none evaluated: a sound literal prefilter that proves no alternative can match before running Pattern; screening each retained byte field once per verify rather than raw plus base64; avoiding the masked copy in writerMatches when no PASS marker is present. Any change is security-sensitive: it must not reduce what is detected.
title: secretscreen: Pattern scans at about 1 microsecond per byte and receipt verification rescans the same bytes
